classification.difficultyReason: Counts colour restrictions using products and mutually exclusive colour cases.

content.prompt: A bag contains three red, seven yellow and five blue balls. If three balls are drawn from the bag simultaneously, find the probability that:

answer.worked:
Choose three of the seven yellow balls. There are $\binom{15}{3}$ possible selections.
$$\begin{aligned}P&=\frac{\binom{7}{3}}{\binom{15}{3}}\\&=\frac{35}{455}\\&=\frac{1}{13}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: all the balls are of the same colour,

answer.worked:
The disjoint cases are three red, three yellow or three blue balls.
$$\begin{aligned}P&=\frac{\binom{3}{3}+\binom{7}{3}+\binom{5}{3}}{\binom{15}{3}}\\&=\frac{1+35+10}{455}\\&=\frac{46}{455}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: there are two red balls and one blue ball,

answer.worked:
Choose two of the three red balls and one of the five blue balls.
$$\begin{aligned}P&=\frac{\binom{3}{2}\times\binom{5}{1}}{\binom{15}{3}}\\&=\frac{15}{455}\\&=\frac{3}{91}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: all the balls are of different colours.

answer.worked:
Choose one red, one yellow and one blue ball.
$$\begin{aligned}P&=\frac{\binom{3}{1}\times\binom{7}{1}\times\binom{5}{1}}{\binom{15}{3}}\\&=\frac{105}{455}\\&=\frac{3}{13}\end{aligned}$$
